# git-pull-request

Open PRs that pass each repo's checks on the first try, and never open one until the user has approved the exact wording.

Related skills: `git-branch` (branch name and base), `git-commit` (title uses the same `KEY: Description` standard).

## Hard rule: approval gate

**Nothing is pushed and no PR is created or edited until the user answers yes to the description.**
The user does not want to bother the team with wording that is not right.

1. Draft the title and body.
2. Run the checker (below) and fix every FAIL.
3. Print the base <- head, title, and full body.
4. Ask with `ask_user` using a single boolean field, e.g. `approved`: "Is this PR description good to open?".
5. Anything other than a clear yes counts as no. On no, ask what to change (free text), revise, re-run the checker, and show it again. Repeat until yes.
6. Edits to an existing PR description (`gh pr edit`) go through the same gate.

## Steps

1. Identify the repo (`git rev-parse --show-toplevel`). The workspace repo itself has no PRs; it pushes to `main`.
2. Confirm the branch follows `git-branch` and is not the base branch. If on `develop` or `main`, stop and offer to create a branch.
3. Check for an existing PR: `gh pr list --head "$(git branch --show-current)" --state open`. If one exists, offer to update it instead.
4. Collect facts: `git log origin/<base>..HEAD --oneline`, `git diff origin/<base>...HEAD --stat`, and read the full diff. Describe the whole PR, not the last commit. Pull the Jira ticket if there is one (Atlassian MCP) for motivation.
5. Draft the title and body per the repo rules below.
6. Run the checker:
   ```
   python3 .github/skills/git-pull-request/scripts/check_pr_description.py \
     --repo <repo-dir-name> --title "<title>" --body-file <file or - for stdin>
   ```
   Paths are relative to the workspace root. `[CI]` lines mirror enforced checks; a FAIL there blocks merge. WARN lines are convention only: fix them or explain.
7. Run the approval gate.
8. Only after yes: `git push -u origin HEAD`, then
   ```
   gh pr create --base <base> --title "<title>" --body-file - <<'EOF'
   <body>
   EOF
   ```
   Open as ready, not draft. Report the URL, then `gh pr checks <url>` once.

## Title

Same as `git-commit`: `KEY: Imperative Capitalised description`, no trailing period, at most 72 characters, never type `(#NNNN)` (GitHub appends it).
RIS enforces `^([A-Z]{2,9}-[0-9]{1,6}|NO-TICKET): .*$`; use `NO-TICKET:` only when there truly is no ticket.

## Body writing

- Specific, plain, factual. Name files, keys, and types in backticks.
- Lead with the changes a reviewer will notice first.
- Do not claim tests passed unless you ran them in this session; say what was run.
- Link Jira as `- https://resideo.atlassian.net/browse/ANW-2624`.
- Cross-repo PR references use full URLs or `resideo/repo#N`; a bare `#N` points at the current repo.
- Empty sections: write "None" rather than deleting the section or leaving a placeholder comment.

## Per-repo rules

| Repo | Base | Template headings (keep order) | Enforced |
|---|---|---|---|
| ds-notification-service | `develop` | `### Related Jira tickets`, `### Motivation`, `### Changes`, `### Preconditions, next steps, remaining questions` | `### Motivation` and `### Changes` must be level-3 headings, each with at least 10 letters of real prose (links, empty bullets, and comments do not count) |
| ds-message-template-api | `develop` | same, but `### Significant changes` instead of `### Changes` | same check with `### Significant changes`; PR must **not be draft** so the template validation workflows run |
| notification-definitions | `main` | `## Jira ticket`, `## What changed`, `## Missing info / follow-up` | none by CI; fill every section, "None" if empty |
| integration-services | `develop` | `## Originating Jira Item`, `## Motivation` | title regex above, and the body must link `https://resideo.atlassian.net/browse/KEY` unless the title starts with `NO-TICKET:`. For non-trivial diffs also add a `## Changes` section. |
| ds-event-definitions | `main` | no template; use the NS structure | nothing; no CODEOWNERS, so ask who should review |

Notes:
- template-api: a workflow writes an `<!-- AUTOGENERATED_SECTION_START/END -->` "Modified Templates" block and applies the `template update` label. Never hand-write those markers or that label.
- notification-definitions: if action `src` changed, `dist/index.js` must be rebuilt and committed before the PR (see `git-commit`).
- RIS: migration paths trigger `validate-db-migrations.yaml`; mention migrations in Motivation.

## Reviewers and labels

- Do not request reviewers: CODEOWNERS adds them (except ds-event-definitions, where you ask).
- Labels are optional. Observed ones: template-api `testing`, `refactoring`; NS `tool`, `chore`, `testing`, `enhancement`; notification-definitions `tooling`, `consistency`, `bug`. RIS and ds-event-definitions use none. Only add one if it clearly fits, and mention it in the approval summary.
- Never set `Do not merge`, `DO NOT MERGE`, or `FORCE QA DEPLOYMENT`.

## Before drafting, verify locally

- NS / template-api: `dotnet build <project>.csproj --no-restore` then `dotnet test <testproject>.csproj --no-build` (warnings are errors).
- notification-definitions: its own validation workflows run on every PR; run its local validate script if present.

## Example (template-api)

Title: `ANW-2685: Set SensorOffline severity to Medium`

```
### Related Jira tickets
- https://resideo.atlassian.net/browse/ANW-2685

### Motivation
The mobile activity feed showed SensorOffline as Urgent (red) while `notification-definitions/templates/Thermostats/sensoroffline.json` specifies Medium.

### Significant changes
- `ActivityFeedTemplates.resx`: `SensorOffline_Severity` returns `Medium` when Status is Active (was `High`).
- `SensorOffline.cs` integration test now expects `Medium`.

### Preconditions, next steps, remaining questions
None
```
